q8.answer: Two guards. First, the commit step dedupes staged rows with ROW_NUMBER() per order_id ordered by updated_at DESC, keeping only the latest. Second, the MERGE updates a matched row only when s.updated_at > t.updated_at, so an older or identical copy never overwrites a newer one. Re-runs and overlapping nights therefore change nothing.

q9.answer: It lives in the warehouse, in etl.control (one row per pipeline, column high_water_mark). It is written inside the commit transaction, in the same transaction as the MERGE and the run_log committed status. The value is GREATEST(current HWM, max updated_at of the rows staged for this run), never the wall clock. It is skipped if staging is empty.

q10.answer: The merge into dw.orders, the HWM update and the run_log status change all happen in one warehouse transaction, so dashboards see either the old data or the finished night. Staging is a separate table that dashboards never read. If the load isn't committed by 06:00, dashboards keep the last committed state and a staleness alert is posted.

q11.answer: Leftover staged rows from the failed attempt stay in stg.orders_extract until the next attempt starts. It first deletes all leftover staged rows from earlier failed attempts, which is safe because the run lease means no other attempt is using staging. It then loads under a new run_id. The retry reads the same HWM, since a failed attempt never advanced it, so it extracts the same window (HWM minus 2 hours) and redoes the whole run. It keeps the original run_date.

q12.answer: For each creation-day (UTC date of created_at) in the last 30 days where the replica and warehouse count or checksum differ, it re-reads every row of that day from the replica, not only the changed ones. These rows are staged under a recon run_id. They are applied with the same dedupe and MERGE as the nightly load (newer updated_at wins), in one transaction covering all mismatched days. It does not touch the nightly HWM. It writes recon_log and deletes the staged rows.
